newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends rollercoaster session firmer.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends rollercoaster session firmer.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended modestly higher in whiplash trading on Thursday, bolstered by a late-session round of local buying, dealers said.
Although the market managed to claw its way back into positive territory in the afternoon, cocoa prices finished well off session highs set earlier in the day.
Benchmark September peaked at $1,722 a tonne, but closed at $1,690, up $7 on the day. Spot July ended $9 higher, at $1,660, while the back months gained $3 to $11.

New York cocoa softened at the outset, defying pre-opening expectations, as traders followed through on Wednesday weak close, dealers said. But light industry-related buying stemmed losses and prompted the ring to cover short positions.
Upward momentum accelerated after the September contract pierced resistance at $1,698-$1,700, touching off buy-stops and sparking speculative interest.
The rally, however, ran into some trade selling and quickly retraced, with September tumbling to a session low of $1,670 before it managed to recover.

Traders said after today's wild ride, sentiment on the floor was uncertain. "The mood is indecisive," said one trader. "People are looking for a reason to get long or a reason to get short. They are being cautious, trying to be nimble. No one wants to be married to a position."
"The fact that specs are holding a long position makes it vunerable each time it dips," another trader said. "The market should go down, but technically it still looks positive."
On the charts, traders pegged near-term support in the September contract at today's low of $1,670, followed by $1,660 and then $1,654. Resistance was seen near $1,700.
Volume was heavy, at an estimated 15,665 lots, but traders said crosses and switches accounted for at least a third of the day's turnover.
